# Prompt Wizard

## Summary
A prompt built one question at a time. Each step asks for one detail — who it's for, what tone, what to include — as a set of choices or a short text answer, while a live preview shows the prompt taking shape. The last step shows the finished prompt, editable, before it runs. It turns a blank box into a short, focused conversation for tasks where a good result needs several details people wouldn't think to give.

## When to use
- Complex requests with a known recipe: job posts, briefs, campaign copy, image prompts, research plans.
- People who are new to the task or to AI, and would write a one-line prompt and get a generic answer.
- When each detail has a small set of good answers that can be offered as choices.

## When not to use
- Quick requests that fit in one sentence; a wizard in front of them is pure friction.
- When people already know what they want and type fast — offer Prompt Template, which shows every blank at once on one line.
- When the questions depend on the request itself and can't be known in advance — use Clarifying Questions after the prompt is sent.
- More than about six steps. Split the task, or move rare details into an optional "Anything else?" step.

## Anatomy
- Header: the task name and "Step 2 of 5", with a segmented progress bar (one segment per step plus review).
- Step body: the question, an optional hint, and either choice chips (single choice) or a short text field. Optional steps are labelled.
- "Prompt so far": a muted, clamped line showing the prompt built from the answers given so far.
- Footer: Back, and Next (Skip on an empty optional step, Review on the last step).
- Review step: the answers as chips that jump back to their step, the full prompt in an editable field, and the run button.

## Behavior
- One question per screen. Steps slide in the direction of travel: forward from the right, back from the left.
- Clicking a choice selects it and moves to the next step after a short beat, so the selection registers before the screen changes. Arrow keys move the selection without advancing; Next confirms.
- Text steps advance with Enter or Next; Shift+Enter adds a new line. Next is disabled until a required step has an answer.
- Back keeps every answer. Going back and changing one rebuilds the prompt everywhere.
- The prompt is built by the product, not the model, so the preview updates instantly and exactly matches what will run.
- On review, the prompt can be edited by hand. A hand edit is kept until an answer changes or the person chooses "Rebuild from answers", so nothing they typed is overwritten silently.
- Running submits the reviewed prompt and the structured answers, which the host can store for "run again" or a template.

## Content guidelines
- Ask questions the way a colleague would: "How senior?", "What will they work on first?". Avoid form labels like "Seniority level".
- Keep choices to three to five short options. Put the most common first, and don't pre-select one.
- Give text steps a concrete example placeholder ("e.g. Redesign onboarding for our mobile app") rather than an instruction.
- Title the review step plainly ("Here's your prompt") and label the run button with the outcome ("Generate", "Write post").

## Accessibility
- The wizard is a labelled region named by the current question; the step counter is a polite live region.
- Focus moves to the new step's input or selected choice after each transition, and never on first load.
- Choices are a `radiogroup` with roving tab index: arrow keys move and select, and Space or Enter picks.
- Text steps are labelled by their question and described by their hint.
- Review chips say which step they change ("Change How senior?: Senior").
- Slides become plain fades, and the auto-advance is immediate, when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Related patterns
- **Prompt Template** — Use it instead to show the whole prompt as one sentence with blanks, for people who want to see everything at once.
- **Clarifying Questions** — Use it instead when the AI works out what to ask after reading the request.
- **Prompt Quality Meter** — Use it instead to coach a free-form prompt without forcing a sequence.
- **Setup Checklist** — Use it for multi-step product setup; this pattern is for one request.

## Default implementation (Tailwind v4 + Radix + Motion)

This is the catalogue's own reference implementation — use it verbatim when the
host project has no established design system, or when the user asks for
"the demoed look." When the host project has its own design system, treat
this code as a translation reference: keep every rule from the spec above
(Anatomy, Behavior, Content guidelines, Accessibility) and re-express the
markup, styling, and motion using that system's own components/tokens
instead of copying these Tailwind classes or the Motion API.

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { AnimatePresence, motion, useReducedMotion } from "motion/react";
import { ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Sparkles } from "lucide-react";

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

export interface WizardStep {
  id: string;
  /** The question for this step: "Who is it for?" */
  question: string;
  hint?: string;
  /** Turns the step into a single choice. Without it, the step is free text. */
  options?: string[];
  placeholder?: string;
  optional?: boolean;
  /** Pre-filled answer. */
  value?: string;
}

export type WizardAnswers = Record<string, string>;

export interface PromptWizardProps {
  title?: string;
  steps: WizardStep[];
  /** Assembles the prompt from the answers so far; also drives the live preview. */
  build: (answers: WizardAnswers) => string;
  onSubmit: (prompt: string, answers: WizardAnswers) => void;
  submitLabel?: string;
  className?: string;
}

export function PromptWizard({ title, steps, build, onSubmit, submitLabel = "Generate", className }: PromptWizardProps) {
  const [index, setIndex] = React.useState(0);
  const [direction, setDirection] = React.useState(1);
  const [answers, setAnswers] = React.useState<WizardAnswers>(() =>
    Object.fromEntries(steps.map((s) => [s.id, s.value ?? ""]))
  );
  // The reviewed prompt, once the person edits it by hand; null means "follow the answers".
  const [edited, setEdited] = React.useState<string | null>(null);
  const advanceTimer = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(undefined);
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const uid = React.useId();

  const reviewing = index === steps.length;
  const step = steps[index];
  const answer = step ? (answers[step.id] ?? "").trim() : "";
  const canContinue = reviewing || step.optional || answer.length > 0;
  const prompt = edited ?? build(answers);

  React.useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(advanceTimer.current), []);

  // Move focus into each new step as it mounts, so keyboard and
  // screen-reader users land on it — but only after a navigation, never on
  // first render.
  const pendingFocus = React.useRef(false);
  const focusStep = React.useCallback((node: HTMLDivElement | null) => {
    if (!node || !pendingFocus.current) return;
    pendingFocus.current = false;
    node.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-autofocus]")?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  }, []);

  function go(next: number) {
    clearTimeout(advanceTimer.current);
    pendingFocus.current = true;
    setDirection(next > index ? 1 : -1);
    setIndex(Math.max(0, Math.min(steps.length, next)));
  }

  function setAnswer(id: string, value: string) {
    setAnswers((prev) => ({ ...prev, [id]: value }));
    setEdited(null);
  }

  function next() {
    if (!canContinue) return;
    if (reviewing) onSubmit(prompt.trim(), answers);
    else go(index + 1);
  }

  const offset = reduceMotion ? 0 : 24;

  return (
    <section
      aria-labelledby={`${uid}-question`}
      className={cn("flex w-full flex-col gap-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl bg-card p-4 shadow-sm ring-1 ring-black/5 dark:ring-white/10", className)}
    >
      <header className="flex flex-col gap-2">
        <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
          <span className="font-medium">{title}</span>
          <span aria-live="polite">{reviewing ? "Review" : `Step ${index + 1} of ${steps.length}`}</span>
        </div>
        <div className="flex gap-1" aria-hidden>
          {[...steps, null].map((s, i) => (
            <span key={s?.id ?? "review"} className="relative h-1 flex-1 overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted">
              <motion.span
                className="absolute inset-0 origin-left rounded-full bg-foreground"
                initial={false}
                animate={{ scaleX: i <= index ? 1 : 0 }}
                transition={{ duration: reduceMotion ? 0 : 0.3, ease: "easeOut" }}
              />
            </span>
          ))}
        </div>
      </header>

      <div className="relative min-h-36">
        <AnimatePresence mode="wait" initial={false} custom={direction}>
          <motion.div
            key={index}
            ref={focusStep}
            custom={direction}
            initial={{ opacity: 0, x: direction * offset }}
            animate={{ opacity: 1, x: 0 }}
            exit={{ opacity: 0, x: direction * -offset }}
            transition={{ duration: 0.2, ease: "easeOut" }}
            className="flex flex-col gap-3"
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              // Enter answers a free-text step; Shift+Enter is a new line. Choice
              // chips are buttons, so Enter already picks them, and the review
              // textarea keeps Enter for line breaks.
              if (e.key === "Enter" && !e.shiftKey && !reviewing && e.target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement) {
                e.preventDefault();
                next();
              }
            }}
          >
            {reviewing ? (
              <>
                <h3 id={`${uid}-question`} className="text-base font-medium">
                  Here&apos;s your prompt
                </h3>
                <ul className="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5" aria-label="Your answers">
                  {steps.map((s, i) => (
                    <li key={s.id}>
                      <button
                        type="button"
                        onClick={() => go(i)}
                        className="rounded-full px-2.5 py-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-foreground/10 hover:text-foreground bg-muted"
                      >
                        <span className="sr-only">Change {s.question}: </span>
                        {answers[s.id]?.trim() || "Skipped"}
                      </button>
                    </li>
                  ))}
                </ul>
                <textarea
                  data-autofocus
                  value={prompt}
                  onChange={(e) => setEdited(e.target.value)}
                  rows={4}
                  aria-label="Prompt"
                  className="resize-none rounded-2xl px-3 py-2 text-sm leading-relaxed outline-none focus:ring-1 focus:ring-foreground/30 bg-muted focus:bg-background"
                />
                {edited !== null && (
                  <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                    Edited by hand.{" "}
                    <button type="button" onClick={() => setEdited(null)} className="font-medium text-foreground underline-offset-2 hover:underline">
                      Rebuild from answers
                    </button>
                  </p>
                )}
              </>
            ) : (
              <>
                <div className="flex flex-col gap-1">
                  <h3 id={`${uid}-question`} className="text-base font-medium">
                    {step.question}
                    {step.optional && <span className="ml-1.5 text-xs font-normal text-muted-foreground">Optional</span>}
                  </h3>
                  {step.hint && (
                    <p id={`${uid}-hint`} className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
                      {step.hint}
                    </p>
                  )}
                </div>

                {step.options ? (
                  <Choices
                    labelledBy={`${uid}-question`}
                    options={step.options}
                    value={answers[step.id] ?? ""}
                    onChange={(v) => setAnswer(step.id, v)}
                    onPick={(v) => {
                      setAnswer(step.id, v);
                      // A click is a decision: move on after the selection registers.
                      clearTimeout(advanceTimer.current);
                      advanceTimer.current = setTimeout(() => go(index + 1), reduceMotion ? 0 : 220);
                    }}
                  />
                ) : (
                  <textarea
                    data-autofocus
                    value={answers[step.id] ?? ""}
                    onChange={(e) => setAnswer(step.id, e.target.value)}
                    placeholder={step.placeholder}
                    aria-labelledby={`${uid}-question`}
                    aria-describedby={step.hint ? `${uid}-hint` : undefined}
                    rows={2}
                    className="resize-none rounded-2xl px-3 py-2 text-sm leading-relaxed outline-none placeholder:text-muted-foreground focus:ring-1 focus:ring-foreground/30 bg-muted focus:bg-background"
                  />
                )}
              </>
            )}
          </motion.div>
        </AnimatePresence>
      </div>

      {!reviewing && (
        <p className="line-clamp-2 border-t pt-3 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
          <span className="font-medium text-foreground">Prompt so far: </span>
          {prompt || "…"}
        </p>
      )}

      <footer className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => go(index - 1)}
          disabled={index === 0}
          className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full px-2.5 py-1.5 text-sm text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground disabled:invisible"
        >
          <ArrowLeft className="size-3.5" aria-hidden />
          Back
        </button>
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={next}
          disabled={!canContinue || (reviewing && !prompt.trim())}
          className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full bg-foreground px-3.5 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-background transition-opacity disabled:opacity-30"
        >
          {reviewing ? (
            <>
              <Sparkles className="size-3.5" aria-hidden />
              {submitLabel}
            </>
          ) : (
            <>
              {step.optional && !answer ? "Skip" : index === steps.length - 1 ? "Review" : "Next"}
              <ArrowRight className="size-3.5" aria-hidden />
            </>
          )}
        </button>
      </footer>
    </section>
  );
}

/** A single-choice radio group of chips with roving focus. */
function Choices({
  labelledBy,
  options,
  value,
  onChange,
  onPick,
}: {
  labelledBy: string;
  options: string[];
  value: string;
  onChange: (value: string) => void;
  onPick: (value: string) => void;
}) {
  const refs = React.useRef<(HTMLButtonElement | null)[]>([]);
  const selected = options.indexOf(value);
  const focusable = selected >= 0 ? selected : 0;

  function onKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent, i: number) {
    const keys: Record<string, number> = { ArrowRight: 1, ArrowDown: 1, ArrowLeft: -1, ArrowUp: -1 };
    if (e.key in keys) {
      e.preventDefault();
      const n = (i + keys[e.key] + options.length) % options.length;
      onChange(options[n]);
      refs.current[n]?.focus();
    } else if (e.key === " ") {
      e.preventDefault();
      onChange(options[i]);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby={labelledBy} className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {options.map((option, i) => {
        const on = option === value;
        return (
          <button
            key={option}
            ref={(el) => {
              refs.current[i] = el;
            }}
            type="button"
            role="radio"
            aria-checked={on}
            tabIndex={i === focusable ? 0 : -1}
            data-autofocus={i === focusable ? true : undefined}
            onClick={() => onPick(option)}
            onKeyDown={(e) => onKeyDown(e, i)}
            className={cn(
              "rounded-full px-3 py-1.5 text-sm transition-colors bg-muted",
              on ? "bg-foreground text-background" : "hover:bg-foreground/10"
            )}
          >
            {option}
          </button>
        );
      })}
    </div>
  );
}
```
